items.q: In the respiratory physiology infographic, by what mechanism does pulmonary surfactant prevent alveolar collapse at low lung volumes according to Laplace law (P = 2T/r)?
o: By increasing alveolar radius proportionally during expiration
By lowering surface tension more dramatically in smaller alveoli
By decreasing intrapleural pressure below -15 cm H2O
By increasing bronchial smooth muscle tone
items.exp: According to Laplace law (P = 2T/r), a smaller radius increases collapsing pressure if surface tension (T) remains constant. Surfactant molecules concentrate more densely on the surface of shrinking alveoli during expiration, lowering surface tension proportionally and thereby equalizing collapsing pressures across varying alveolar sizes.
r: Incorrect. Alveolar radius decreases during expiration.
Correct. Surfactant molecules concentrate in smaller alveoli, lowering surface tension and stabilizing them.
Incorrect. Surfactant acts on surface tension, not by hyper-negativizing intrapleural pressure.
Incorrect. Bronchial smooth muscle tone does not regulate alveolar collapsing pressure.
items.kp: Surfactant concentrates in smaller alveoli, lowering surface tension and preventing diffuse atelectasis.
